title: Revive worker failure-circuit and per-tenant dynamic concurrency for streaming queues
creator: Leah Park
description: Problem: Our Redis/Kafka stream consumers are still relying on a brittle global retry budget and exponential backoff that causes noisy hotspots and long tails during tenant traffic bursts. Several incidents in Q3/Q4 showed cascading retries, overloaded workers, and high p99 latency when one tenant had a malformed workload. Goal: Replace the global retry/backoff approach with a per-tenant token-bucket based retry guard and introduce a failure-circuit short-circuiting mechanism plus a dynamic concurrency controller that adapts worker concurrency per-tenant based on real-time latency and error signals. This reduces cascading retries, improves tail latency, and makes graceful shedding predictable. Scope: worker pool code (stream consumer), retry orchestration, lease/lock semantics, Redis client upgrade, new metrics/tracing, and canary rollout for high-volume tenants. Not in scope: application-level message semantics changes and schema migrations for payloads.

acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant token bucket enforces retry budgets and shows expected rejects in metrics
Failure-circuit short-circuits processing for an unhealthy worker-group within 60s of elevated error-rate
Dynamic concurrency controller increases/decreases per-tenant concurrency automatically without global regressions
Redis client upgrade passes stability matrix (connections, pipelining, reconnects)
No >10% adverse change on p50/p95/p99 for unaffected tenants during canary
Feature flag allows immediate disable and full rollback within 15 minutes
notes: Trade-offs: token-bucket per-tenant requires storing counters in Redis with O(1) ops; slightly higher Redis QPS but much improved isolation. We considered a pure in-memory approach but it fails across multi-replica consumers.
Failure-circuit: modeled after circuit-breaker, but state transitions include 'throttled' to allow low-rate probes instead of full open/closed. This reduces noisy restarts.
Concurrency controller: fast-path uses EWMA of latency+error to probe up; probe cadence tuned to avoid oscillation. Tunables exposed via console for enterprise tenants.
Dependency: moving to redis.asyncio 4.5 removes deprecated API calls used by aioredis; requires CI images to include Python 3.10+ builds.
Security: no customer data changes. KMS/HSM integration not impacted. Security review not required for this change but observability data should avoid storing full payloads.
